The designed HTP steel was smelted in a vacuum furnace, cast into ingots (700 mm × 100 mm × 100 mm), and cut into bars of 120 mm × 100 mm × 100 mm for subsequent experimental procedures.

other.mill: 450 mm two-roll reversing hot rolling mill

evidence.quote: The bars were rolled to a thickness of 12 mm by a 450 mm two-roll reversing hot rolling mill and cooled to room temperature. A two-stage controlled rolling process was adopted. The rolling temperature in the austenite recrystallization and non-recrystallization zones were 1050-1150 °C and 890-900 °C, respectively.
After rolling, the steel plate was reheated to 890 °C for 40 min to ensure complete austenitization, and then quenched to room temperature.
It was again reheated to 200 °C for 40 min for tempering and cooled to room temperature to obtain the HTP experimental steel plate.
The microstructure of HTP steel, obtained by quenching and tempering, was determined to be primarily lath martensite.
the martensite packet was composed of multiple laths, which were generally arranged in parallel to each other, and ε carbides were distributed in the martensite matrix
Fig. 3a shows a martensite packet in the original austenite grains, and the austenite grain boundaries are clearly visible in the microstructure.
